comparison: Both evaluate ASCT2 as a d-serine transporter (C62-C69) and its functional validation (C70-C71). OpenEval provides detailed assessment of proteomics, immunofluorescence, and transport assays. Peer reviewers affirm this as 'convincing' with 'compelling evidence.' Both find the evidence SUPPORTED with no concerns raised.

OpenEval R6 addresses functional validation of ASCT2 (C70-C71) using knockout and knockdown approaches. Peer R1 includes these claims as part of broader ASCT2 characterization. Both evaluations are SUPPORTED and complementary.

OpenEval R10 covers SMCT functional validation with d-serine (C91-C96), while Peer R2 addresses broader SMCT transport characterization (C91-C109). Both find evidence SUPPORTED. Peer reviewers note 'it's clear SMCTs can transport D-serine' and accept the comprehensive characterization.

OpenEval R11 evaluates radiotracer uptake assays for SMCT-mediated d-serine transport (C97-C100). Peer R2 includes these claims in broader SMCT characterization. Both evaluations are SUPPORTED with acceptance of the functional evidence.

OpenEval R14 assesses proteoliposome characterization of SMCT transport (C104-C109). Peer R2 encompasses these claims in overall SMCT transport validation. Both find the cell-free system evidence SUPPORTED and accept the comprehensive characterization.
OpenEval R12 evaluates kinetics analysis for d-serine transport (C101). Peer R2 includes kinetic characterization as part of detailed SMCT transport evidence. Both evaluations are SUPPORTED.

Both evaluate amino acid profiling during IRI (C39-C44, C112-C113). OpenEval finds 2D-HPLC measurements well-supported with appropriate analytical methods. Peer reviewers accept these metabolomics findings as demonstrating 'the value of D-serine as a potential marker of renal injury.' Both are SUPPORTED.

Both address urinary d-serine changes during IRI (C48-C50, C113). OpenEval finds the decreased urinary d-/l-serine ratios well-supported. Peer reviewers accept these findings as part of the metabolomics validation. Both evaluations are SUPPORTED.

Both evaluate proteomics methodology and findings (C52-C58). OpenEval assesses mass spectrometry data and validation through known AKI biomarkers. Peer reviewers accept the proteomics approach and note improvements in linking proteomics to transporter selection. Both are SUPPORTED.

OpenEval R4 evaluates IPA pathway analysis (C59-C61). Peer R5 addresses broader proteomics findings including transporter expression patterns. Both find the proteomics-based transporter categorization SUPPORTED, though OpenEval notes compensatory mechanism interpretation is somewhat speculative.

Both address transcriptomics data integration (C128-C130). OpenEval finds snRNA-seq analysis supportive but notes mechanistic conclusions are somewhat inferential. Peer reviewers accept the transcriptomics integration as strengthening the manuscript. Both are SUPPORTED.

Both evaluate ex vivo BBMV transport assays (C114-C119). OpenEval finds the biphasic kinetics and differential inhibitor sensitivity provide strong evidence for two transport systems. Peer reviewers accept the ex vivo transport data as 'compelling evidence.' Both are SUPPORTED.

Both address ex vivo BBMV transport in IRI models (C121-C126). OpenEval finds correlation between transport activity and protein expression well-supported. Peer reviewers accept the ex vivo analyses as part of comprehensive approach. Both are SUPPORTED.

Perfect claim overlap (C72-C81). Both evaluate the rationale for seeking additional transporters beyond ASCT2. OpenEval finds the knowledge gap identification well-reasoned. Peer reviewers implicitly accept this logic as it led to SMCT discovery, with one reviewer noting improved clarity on transporter selection rationale. Both are SUPPORTED.

Both evaluate cell growth assays with d-serine (C85-C88). OpenEval finds concentration-response and stereospecificity data well-characterized. Peer reviewers do not question these findings and consider them part of 'exhaustive methods' providing 'compelling evidence.' Both are SUPPORTED.

Both address nicotinate transport validation in proteoliposomes (C102-C103). OpenEval finds this validates the proteoliposome approach for subsequent d-serine studies. Peer reviewers accept the kinetic characterization as part of comprehensive evidence. Both are SUPPORTED.

OpenEval R18 evaluates structural/kinetic rationale for SMCT-serine interaction (C133-C134). Peer R9 accepts kinetic characterization broadly. Both find the comparison to known substrates appropriate and SUPPORTED.

Both address differential d-serine affinity between SMCT1 and SMCT2 (C135-C136). OpenEval notes the inference is reasonable but qualified. Peer reviewers accept the kinetic characterization without specific concerns. Both are SUPPORTED.

Perfect claim overlap (C137-C141). Both evaluate integration of proteomics and transcriptomics for transporter expression patterns. OpenEval finds inferences about relative contributions reasonable but somewhat speculative. Peer reviewers accept the expression data and functional implications. Both are SUPPORTED.

Both evaluate integration of current findings with nephrotoxicity literature (C143-C146). OpenEval finds the match between transport properties and SMCT characteristics appropriate but notes nephrotoxicity mechanism is speculative. Peer reviewers accept this integration as strengthening connections to existing knowledge. Both are SUPPORTED.

OpenEval R22 synthesizes normal kidney d-serine handling model (C149-C153). Peer R3 evaluates physiological roles with UNCERTAIN status, questioning relative contributions and expression changes. OpenEval finds the model SUPPORTED but notes some inferences are indirect. Divergence in confidence level.

OpenEval R23 addresses pathological d-serine handling model (C154-C157). Peer R3 expresses UNCERTAIN evaluation, questioning how ASCT2 increase with SMCT1 decrease results in increased reabsorption. OpenEval finds model SUPPORTED but somewhat speculative. Peer reviewers initially questioned mechanism but were ultimately satisfied after revision.

OpenEval R15 addresses biphasic kinetics in BBMV (C120). Peer R3 questions relative physiological roles and expression patterns. Minimal overlap but both relate to mechanistic interpretation of transport systems.

OpenEval R16 evaluates ASCT2 dominance during pathology (C127). Peer R3 questions this interpretation with UNCERTAIN status. OpenEval finds it SUPPORTED by correlation of transport and expression data. Divergence in confidence.

Perfect claim overlap (C158-C162). Both evaluate l-serine transport integration into overall model. OpenEval finds the proposal reasonable but notes some inferences are indirect. Peer reviewers accept this integrated model after revision. Both are SUPPORTED.

Perfect claim overlap (C163-C168). Both evaluate ASCT2's broader biological context and role in recovery. OpenEval finds the postulation speculative but reasonable. Peer reviewers accept the transcriptomics integration and mechanistic proposal. Both are SUPPORTED.

OpenEval R8 evaluates rational selection strategy for candidate transporters (C82-C83). No corresponding peer review evaluation found. OpenEval finds the criteria appropriate though involving subjective judgment. SUPPORTED.
